Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)

collisions.mechanism: Additive block of rapid delayed rectifier cardiac potassium currents (IKr / hERG channel), triggering marked QTc prolongation (>500 ms) and precipitate Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (Torsades de Pointes).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Syncope, palpitations, sudden cardiac arrest, ventricular fibrillation.
safer_alternatives: Substitute Azithromycin with Doxycycline or Amoxicillin/Clavulanate for respiratory infections.
If atypical pneumonia coverage is mandatory, conduct daily baseline 12-lead ECG monitoring and maintain serum K+ > 4.5 mEq/L and Mg2+ > 2.0 mg/dL.
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Black Box & ACC/AHA Class III Harm Warning

collisions.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition by Clarithromycin markedly reduces Amiodarone clearance while synergistically prolonging ventricular repolarization (additive hERG channel blockade).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Profound QTc prolongation (>520ms), high risk of fatal Torsades de Pointes, severe bradycardia.
safer_alternatives: Avoid co-administration. Use Cefuroxime, Doxycycline, or Aztreonam as alternative anti-infective therapy.

collisions.mechanism: Both agents cause concentration-dependent QT interval prolongation via potassium channel IKr delay. Co-prescribing elevates TdP risk by >6-fold.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Dizziness, Torsades de Pointes, ventricular tachycardia.
safer_alternatives: Switch antidepressant to Sertraline or Bupropion (lowest QT prolongation risk in class).
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Drug Safety Communication - Avoid Citalopram with QT-prolonging antiarrhythmics

collisions.mechanism: Dual inhibition of hemostasis: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X), while Aspirin irreversibly disables platelet TXA2-mediated aggregation. Gastric mucosal injury compounds bleeding risk.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage, intracranial bleed, hematuria, extensive hematomas.
safer_alternatives: Discontinue Aspirin unless patient has recent PCI/stent within 1-3 months (per 2024 ESC/ACC AFib guidelines, DOAC monotherapy is preferred).
Add Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI: Pantoprazole 40mg daily) for gastroprotection if combination is strictly indicated.

collisions.mechanism: Ibuprofen displaces Warfarin from plasma albumin binding sites and competitively inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism, raising free Warfarin concentrations and INR, while causing direct gastric mucosal erosions.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Massive upper GI bleeding, dangerously elevated INR (>6.0), hemorrhagic stroke.
safer_alternatives: Use Acetaminophen (Paracetamol) up to 2g/day or topical analgesics (Capsaicin, Lidocaine patch).
If anti-inflammatory therapy is critical, consult rheumatology and consider short-course intra-articular corticosteroid.

collisions.mechanism: NSAID antiplatelet effect and GI mucosal injury synergize with Factor Xa inhibition, increasing major bleeding risk 3- to 4-fold without offering antidote titration via INR.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Melena, hematemesis, severe drop in hemoglobin.
safer_alternatives: Acetaminophen 500-1000 mg Q8H PRN, topical NSAID gel (Diclofenac 1% with minimal systemic absorption), or physical therapy.

collisions.mechanism: Potent inhibition of CYP2C9 by Fluconazole blocks the clearance of the more potent S-warfarin enantiomer, causing rapid, severe spike in INR.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: INR doubling within 48 hours, spontaneous epistaxis, gross hematuria, retroperitoneal hematoma.
safer_alternatives: If Fluconazole is unavoidable, preemptively reduce Warfarin dose by 50% and check INR at 48 and 72 hours.
Consider topical antifungal or alternative class where appropriate.

collisions.mechanism: Dual blockade of aldosterone pathway (ACE inhibitor lowers circulating aldosterone; Spironolactone directly blocks mineralocorticoid receptor in distal nephron cortical collecting tubule). Impairs potassium excretion.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Serum K+ > 5.5 - 6.5 mEq/L, peaked T waves, PR prolongation, widening QRS, sine-wave arrest, muscle flaccidity.
safer_alternatives: Monitor serum creatinine & K+ at baseline, 1 week, 4 weeks, and quarterly.
Ensure eGFR > 30 mL/min/1.73m2. Do not exceed Spironolactone 25 mg daily without nephrology co-management.
If K+ rises > 5.5 mEq/L, add potassium binder (Patiromer or Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate).
collisions.regulatory_alert: RALES Trial Warning: Routine K+ & Creatinine surveillance mandatory

collisions.mechanism: Administering exogenous potassium to a patient whose renal potassium excretion is blocked by an MRA is the leading cause of iatrogenic lethal hyperkalemic cardiac arrest.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Lethal ventricular arrhythmias (ventricular fibrillation, asystole) triggered by sudden hyperkalemia (K+ > 6.5 mEq/L).
safer_alternatives: Immediately discontinue Potassium supplements upon initiating Spironolactone or Eplerenone.
Supplement potassium only if documented hypokalemia (< 3.5 mEq/L) occurs despite MRA therapy.

collisions.mechanism: Valsartan ARB component inhibits AT1 receptors while Sacubitril preserves natriuretic peptides, mildly elevating hyperkalemia risk when combined with MRA.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Progressive hyperkalemia, especially in patients with baseline CKD stage 3b+.
safer_alternatives: Titrate cautiously with serial K+ checks every 2 weeks during dose uptitration.
Maintain dietary low-potassium counselling.

collisions.mechanism: Synergistic negative inotropic, chronotropic, and dromotropic depression of the Sinoatrial (SA) and Atrioventricular (AV) nodes. Calcium channel blockade plus beta-adrenergic receptor blockade.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Profound sinus bradycardia (HR < 40 bpm), complete 3rd degree AV block, cardiogenic shock, syncope.
safer_alternatives: Avoid combination. In HFrEF patients, beta-blocker (Carvedilol or Metoprolol Succinate) is mandatory guideline-directed medical therapy; Diltiazem is contraindicated.
If additional rate control is needed in AFib, consider low-dose Digoxin under expert supervision.

collisions.mechanism: Direct additive suppression of AV nodal conduction velocity and myocardial contractility. Verapamil also inhibits metoprolol CYP2D6 clearance.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Severe hemodynamic instability, high-grade AV block, pulmonary edema.
safer_alternatives: Never combine oral Verapamil and Metoprolol in heart failure or conduction disease.
Use Dihydropyridine CCB (Amlodipine) if additional blood pressure reduction is required, as it does not suppress nodal conduction.

collisions.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits renal and biliary P-glycoprotein efflux of Digoxin, doubling serum Digoxin levels, while both agents exert additive negative chronotropic effects on the AV node.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Nausea, xanthopsia (yellow-green halos), ventricular bigeminy, junctional escape rhythm, complete heart block.
safer_alternatives: Immediately reduce Digoxin dose by 50% when initiating Amiodarone.
Obtain baseline and 1-week serum Digoxin level (target 0.5 - 0.8 ng/mL) and frequent ECG rhythm strips.

collisions.mechanism: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (DAPT) produces synergistic inhibition of primary platelet plug formation via both COX-1 and ADP P2Y12 pathways.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Ecchymosis, epistaxis, prolonged bleeding from venipuncture, GI ulceration.
safer_alternatives: Standard guideline indication for 6-12 months post-ACS / Drug-Eluting Stent, but avoid extending beyond recommended duration without explicit ischemic indication.
Add PPI (Pantoprazole) to mitigate gastrointestinal ulceration risk.
collisions.regulatory_alert: DAPT Consensus Guideline Regimen with Bleeding Precaution

collisions.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandin synthesis, causing vasoconstriction of the afferent glomerular arteriole. ACE inhibitors dilate the efferent arteriole. Together, glomerular filtration pressure collapses ('Triple Whammy' risk with diuretics).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Acute kidney injury (abrupt rise in serum creatinine), fluid retention, worsening heart failure, elevated blood pressure.
safer_alternatives: Avoid systemic NSAIDs in all patients with Heart Failure, CKD, or taking ACEi/ARBs.
Utilize non-nephrotoxic analgesics: Acetaminophen or topical therapy.

collisions.primary_hazard: Acute Renal Failure & Decompensated Heart Failure
collisions.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit renal vasodilating prostaglandins (afferent arteriole constriction), while valsartan blocks AT1 vasoconstriction (efferent arteriole dilation), precipitating acute decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Rapid decline in renal function, fluid retention, pulmonary congestion, hyperkalemia.
safer_alternatives: Avoid NSAIDs in all HFrEF patients receiving ARNI therapy.
Use Acetaminophen (Paracetamol) or topical analgesics (Capsaicin / Lidocaine patch).
collisions.regulatory_alert: HFSA / ESC Heart Failure Guideline Warning

collisions.mechanism: Inhibition of renal prostaglandins by NSAIDs blunts furosemide-induced natriuresis and loop diuretic response, while precipitating pre-renal azotemia ('Triple Whammy' with RAAS blockers).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Oliguria, peripheral and pulmonary edema recurrence, acute creatinine surge.
safer_alternatives: Discontinue NSAID; substitute with Acetaminophen.
If congestion worsens, optimize loop diuretic dose under nephrology/cardiology guidance.

collisions.mechanism: Synergistic inhibition of primary platelet aggregation (Aspirin) and secondary coagulation cascade thrombin generation (Factor Xa inhibition by Apixaban).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Major gastrointestinal bleed, intracranial hemorrhage, extensive spontaneous ecchymoses.
safer_alternatives: Per 2024 ESC/AHA guidelines, discontinue Aspirin after 12 months post-ACS/PCI and continue DOAC monotherapy.
Add gastroprotective PPI (Pantoprazole 40mg daily) if dual therapy is temporarily required.

collisions.mechanism: Both agents independently delay ventricular repolarization by blocking human ether-a-go-go-related gene (hERG) K+ channels. Concomitant use causes profound additive QTc prolongation.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (Torsades de Pointes), syncope, sudden cardiac death.
safer_alternatives: Switch antidepressant to Sertraline or Bupropion (lowest arrhythmogenic risk profile in class).
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Drug Safety Advisory: Extreme QTc Risk

collisions.mechanism: Dual suppression of AV nodal conduction velocity and SA node automaticity. Both agents exert negative chronotropic and dromotropic actions.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Symptomatic sinus bradycardia (< 50 bpm), first- or second-degree AV block, fatigue, presyncope.
safer_alternatives: Monitor resting heart rate and ECG PR interval during dose titration.
Target Digoxin serum trough concentration 0.5 - 0.8 ng/mL.

collisions.mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4-mediated Warfarin clearance and eradicates vitamin K-synthesizing intestinal microflora, producing rapid, unpredictable surges in INR and major bleeding risk.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Gross hematuria, gastrointestinal bleeding, spontaneous bruising, INR > 7.0.
safer_alternatives: Avoid macrolides in anticoagulated patients. Use Amoxicillin, Cefuroxime, or Doxycycline for respiratory infections.
If Clarithromycin is strictly necessary, preemptively reduce Warfarin dose by 30-50% and perform INR surveillance every 48 hours.

collisions.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin potently inhibits renal cation transport and CYP3A4, markedly increasing Dofetilide plasma concentrations while exerting additive hERG potassium channel blockade.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Severe QTc prolongation > 550 ms, high risk of fatal Torsades de Pointes and ventricular fibrillation.
safer_alternatives: Absolute contraindication. Use Doxycycline or Cefpodoxime for bacterial infection.
Maintain inpatient continuous telemetry if cardiac antiarrhythmic adjustment is required.
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Boxed Warning — Contraindicated with Dofetilide

collisions.mechanism: Additive inhibition of myocardial delayed rectifier potassium currents (IKr). Both agents independently prolong ventricular action potential duration.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, syncope, sudden cardiac death.
safer_alternatives: Avoid fluoroquinolones. Prescribe Amoxicillin/Clavulanate or Ceftriaxone for respiratory infections.

collisions.mechanism: Naproxen inhibits COX-1 platelete TXA2 and induces gastric mucosal ulceration while displacing Warfarin from protein binding sites, resulting in severe synergistic hemorrhagic diathesis.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Massive upper gastrointestinal bleed, gross hematuria, retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
safer_alternatives: Substitute with Acetaminophen up to 2 g/day. For inflammatory pain, consider topical Lidocaine or consult pain management.

collisions.mechanism: Ketoconazole is a potent P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter inhibitor, increasing Dabigatran bioavailability and peak plasma concentrations by >150%.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Spontaneous major bleeding, hemorrhagic shock, lack of rapid reversal titration.
safer_alternatives: Avoid concomitant systemic ketoconazole with Dabigatran. Use topical antifungal or echinocandins for invasive mycoses.
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Contraindication for Systemic Azoles with Dabigatran

collisions.mechanism: Synergistic osmotic diuresis (SGLT2 glucosuria) and loop natriuresis (Furosemide inhibition of Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of Henle).
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Dehydration, acute prerenal azotemia, orthostatic syncope, dizziness.
safer_alternatives: Down-titrate Furosemide dose by 25-50% when initiating Empagliflozin in euvolemic patients.
Instruct patient on daily weight and blood pressure monitoring.

collisions.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit renal vasodilatory prostaglandins (PGE2/PGI2), constricting afferent arterioles and decreasing GFR. Combined with Spironolactone aldosterone receptor antagonism, renal potassium clearance is blunted, precipitating acute cardiorenal decompensation.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Rapid serum potassium elevation (>6.0 mEq/L), acute oliguria, edema exacerbation, blunting of loop diuretic response.
safer_alternatives: Strictly avoid OTC NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Combiflam) in heart failure patients on MRAs.
Use topical analgesics or low-dose acetaminophen (Paracetamol) up to 2 g/day.
If inflammatory analgesia is unavoidable, perform serial serum potassium & creatinine checks within 48-72 hours.
collisions.regulatory_alert: Black Box Warning: Severe Nephrotoxicity & Hyperkalemia Hazard

collisions.mechanism: Dual blockade of RAAS (Telmisartan blocks AT1 receptor; Spironolactone blocks mineralocorticoid receptor). Impairs distal potassium excretion.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Serum K+ > 5.5 - 6.5 mEq/L, peaked T waves, risk of cardiac arrest in elderly or CKD stage 3b+ patients.
safer_alternatives: Monitor serum creatinine & K+ at baseline, 1 week, and 4 weeks.
Ensure eGFR > 30 mL/min. Do not exceed Spironolactone 25 mg daily without nephrology co-management.
collisions.regulatory_alert: ACC/AHA Class III Harm Warning without strict electrolyte monitoring

collisions.primary_hazard: Acute Renal Failure & Loss of Antihypertensive Efficacy
collisions.mechanism: NSAIDs blunt prostaglandin-mediated afferent arteriolar dilation while ARB blunts angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar constriction, causing trans-glomerular pressure collapse and acute tubular necrosis.
collisions.clinical_manifestation: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), fluid retention, loss of blood pressure control.
safer_alternatives: Discontinue NSAID; substitute Paracetamol.
Monitor renal function and fluid status.
collisions.regulatory_alert: FDA Warning: Concomitant ARB + NSAID triples acute kidney injury rate
